sections.title: Prerequisites And References
sections.text: Select an explicit open Design document and component context (root by default). Mutating execution activates that document, but does not save it. plane accepts XY/XZ/YZ or a native construction-plane/planar-face reference. References are unique names/aliases or {token,kind?,component?,occurrence?}; obtain real references with entity.list or selection.inspect (selected entity is selections[i].entity). component/occurrence are references, not coordinate arrays. occurrence here is an optional creation occurrence passed to addWithoutEdges for cross-component support; it is not an arbitrary placement transform. Fusion validates support compatibility. No base-feature option or automatic edge projection.

sections.title: Return Contract
sections.text: result = {sketch: Ref}. Ref normally has token:string|null, kind:string, name:string|null, optional component:Ref and occurrence:Ref. Root component refs are {kind:component,name:root}; occurrence refs also have path:string. The command envelope has success:boolean, operation:string, document:string, result:object, created:Ref[]. The sketch is appended to created. For batch step s, pass {"$ref":"s.result.sketch"} as the next sketch input. Outside a batch substitute the actual returned object, not $ref syntax.

sections.title: Safety
sections.text: name must be a nonblank string; unknown fields are rejected. Name uniqueness is not enforced here: inspect existing sketches before creation and prefer returned refs over ambiguous names. Creation/naming/serialization failures can leave a sketch; inspect before retry. Offline validation does not certify planar supports or kernel feasibility.

examples.label: Origin sketch
examples.requires: An open Design and native component context. Ensure Section is unused if later using name-based examples.
examples.output: Use result.sketch as sketch.geometry.sketch; no geometry is created yet.

verified: Full schema and occurrence argument
Empty sketch return and naming behavior

sections.title: Discovery And Scope
sections.text: sketch is a unique sketch name/alias or returned {token,kind,component?,occurrence?} reference; entity.list with {kind:sketch} returns entities to select. No activation or recompute occurs. Native results use component coordinates; explicit proxies retain occurrence context. Reinspect after geometry edits before using profile indices.

sections.title: Return Contract
sections.text: result has sketch:Ref, isFullyConstrained:boolean, curves:Description[], points:Description[], constraints:Ref[], dimensions:[{ref:Ref,expression:string,isDriving:boolean}], profiles:[{ref:{kind:profile,sketch:Ref,index:integer},loops:integer}]. Ref has token:string|null, kind:string, name:string|null and optional component/occurrence refs (occurrences also path). Description adds objectType:string and API-available isValid/isVisible/isSolid/isSuppressed booleans, errorOrWarningMessage:string, healthState:{value:integer,name:string}, boundingBox:{min:number[3],max:number[3],units:cm}, geometry:object|null, area/volume/length:{value:number,units:string}. Geometry has type,lengthUnits:cm,angleUnits:rad,space and available origin/center/normal/axis/direction/startPoint/endPoint/xyz number[3] or radius/majorRadius/minorRadius/halfAngle/startAngle/endAngle numbers. Fields depend on entity type, not a uniform curve schema. Coordinates are evaluated snapshots, not equations. Envelope is {success,operation,document,result,created}; created is empty. Batch i.result.profiles.0.ref can feed model.extrude.profile; i.result.curves.0 can feed entity.inspect.ref. Profile refs intentionally omit tokens.

examples.label: Inspect section
examples.requires: Create Section with sketch.create and add geometry first to obtain meaningful profiles.
examples.output: Select a profile from result.profiles by inspected loops/geometry; do not assume index 0 remains stable.

verified: Every return array and conditional description field
Profile selector wiring and snapshot units

sections.title: GM06 Controlled Edits
sections.text: Alternative to legacy fields: movePoints:[{point:RefOrEndpointSelector,to:[x,y,0]}] and/or dimensions:[{dimension:Ref,expression}]; optional frame:sketch. These cannot combine with legacy name/visible/entities/construction/fixed/delete fields. Negative and zero point targets are preserved. Moves use SketchPoint.move and reject fixed/reference/fully constrained points; other solver conflicts return fail. Dimension edits require existing native driving dimensions, including separate ellipse major/minor radius dimensions. Final ellipse sizes are validated together and writes ordered to avoid axis inversion. GM06 result adds schemaVersion:1, status/documentIdentity/units/frame/associativity, before/after, affected and conflicts. Moves are snapshot edits, dimension expressions persistent. No constraint deletion or rollback; see docs/GM06.md. Native acceptance remains open.

sections.title: Selection And Safety
sections.text: sketch accepts a unique name or Ref. Obtain entities from sketch.inspect curves/points, sketch.geometry entities/refs, or selection.inspect selections[i].entity. Ref is {token,kind?,component?,occurrence?} or a unique existing alias; endpoints may be {entity:curveRef,point:start|end|center}. Every selected entity must belong to this sketch. construction/fixed/delete keys require nonempty entities even if false. All flags must be JSON booleans. delete:true requires confirm:true and excludes even construction:false/fixed:false. delete:false performs ordinary edits. No name/visible/entities action is mandatory beyond sketch; a no-op is accepted. Rename/visibility occur before per-entity edits; later solver/deletion failures can leave partial edits. No rollback, save or plane replacement.

sections.title: Return Contract
sections.text: result = {sketch:Ref,edited:integer}; edited is selected entity count, not changed-property count. Ref has token:string|null,kind:string,name:string|null and optional component/occurrence refs. Deleted entity refs are not returned. Envelope {success,operation,document,result,created} has created:[]; batch e.result.sketch is usable by sketch.inspect. No deletion undo token is returned.

examples.label: Show sketch
examples.requires: Existing unique Section sketch in the target document.
examples.output: result.edited is 0; visibility is updated.

examples.label: Delete discovered curve
examples.requires: SeedLine must be an existing entity.alias for a curve from sketch.inspect Section; inspect its dependents before deletion. This is not a built-in curve name.
examples.output: result.edited is 1 if deletion succeeds; dependent constraints may also disappear.

verified: Boolean presence versus truth conditions
Mutation ordering and edited count

sections.title: GM06 Ellipses And Preflight
sections.text: Ellipse adds {type:ellipse,center,majorRadius,minorRadius,angle?} OR {type:ellipse,center,majorAxisPoint,minorAxisPoint}. Endpoints must be perpendicular, nonzero, with major radius > minor radius. Radius means half the full axis length. Ellipse points are planar sketch-local XY even on XZ/YZ support. Optional frame:sketch and inferencePolicy:explicit(default)|native preserve SDK constraints without changing global preferences or deleting constraints. The full geometry list's fields and coordinate expressions are validated before creation; kernel failures may still leave partial geometry. Existing spatial points/lines/splines remain supported. Result also carries GM06 schemaVersion/status/documentIdentity/units/frame/associativity:snapshot/provenance; see docs/GM06.md.

sections.title: Nested Geometry
sections.text: geometry is a nonempty array. Each object requires type and exactly its fields: point:{point}; line/rectangle:{start,end}; circle:{center,radius}; arc:{center,start,sweep}; arc3:{start,through,end}; spline:{points}, at least two points; bezier:{controlPoints}, exactly four PointExpr arrays ordered start, first handle, second handle, end. Optional name is a nonblank unique response label, construction:boolean is prohibited on points, fixed:boolean sets fixed state except for bezier. Every coordinate is exactly three length-expression strings, including zero with units, in sketch coordinates. Use mm/cm/in or existing length parameters; sweep is an angle expression such as 90 deg. Numeric coordinates are not accepted. Expressions are evaluated to cm/rad once, not retained as equations. Add sketch.dimension and constraints for persistent driving editable geometry; fixed geometry is not parametric sizing.

sections.title: Exact Cubic Bezier
sections.text: bezier creates an exact nonrational degree-3 NurbsCurve3D with knots [0,0,0,0,1,1,1,1] and isPeriodic=false, imported by sketchFixedSplines.addByNurbsCurve. The result is a SketchFixedSpline: an intrinsically fixed noneditable reference curve, not a fitted approximation or editable control-point spline. fixed:true or omitted is valid; fixed:false rejects before any geometry is added. construction retains the ordinary curve convention and may be true or false. Control-point expressions are creation-time snapshots, not persistent equations. No generalized NURBS schema or editable handles are provided.

sections.title: Return Contract
sections.text: result = {entities:Ref[],refs:{label:Ref|Ref[]}} in creation order. Rectangle label maps to four curve refs; all other labels map to one ref. Ref has token:string|null,kind:string,name:string|null and optional component/occurrence refs. Names here do not rename or alias native curves. Envelope {success,operation,document,result,created} appends created geometry refs. Batch g.result.refs.rim can feed a dimension entities element; g.result.refs.box.0 selects the first rectangle edge. Outside batches use the actual reference object.

sections.title: Prerequisites And Safety
sections.text: Create/discover the native target sketch via sketch.create result.sketch or entity.list {kind:sketch}. A unique name works. GM06 prevalidates the whole list before creation; kernel feasibility is not established offline. No automatic rollback, repair or profile selection. Circles/rectangles/ellipses are sketch-XY primitives; conic/slot/editable-control-point-spline modes remain unsupported.

examples.label: Named circle
examples.requires: Existing Section sketch; use a fresh sketch to avoid overlap.
examples.output: result.refs.rim is the circle ref for sketch.dimension entities[0]; center selector is {entity:thatRef,point:center}.

examples.label: Rectangle and fitted spline
examples.requires: Fresh Section sketch. Spline is construction geometry and will not bound a solid profile.
examples.output: result.refs.box contains four refs; result.refs.guide is one fitted-spline ref.

examples.label: Exact cubic artwork segment
examples.requires: Existing fresh Section sketch. This is a single open artwork segment, not a closed profile.
examples.output: result.refs.art and result.entities[0] reference the same intrinsically fixed noneditable SketchFixedSpline.

verified: Existing geometry branches and optional flags
Exact cubic Bezier native arguments and unit conversion

sections.title: GM06 Existing Constraint Recognition
sections.text: Native H/V, point alignment, parallel/perpendicular, concentric, equal and coincident constraints are recognized by their documented constrained entities. Requesting the same recognized relation returns its existing constraint ref with reused:true and does not append another constraint. Token aliases are resolved before comparison. Other supported legacy relation types still delegate to the native add method; no total-count inference, automatic constraint deletion or solver repair occurs.

sections.title: Ordered Entities
sections.text: Use refs from sketch.geometry or sketch.inspect; strings must be real unique entity aliases, not geometry response labels. Ref = {token,kind?,component?,occurrence?}. Point selectors are {entity:curveRef,point:start|end|center}, where the curve must expose that point. All subjects must belong to the target sketch. horizontal/vertical take one line; symmetry takes two like entities then an axis line; coincident takes point then point/curve; midpoint takes point then line; perpendicular takes line then curve; collinear/parallel take two lines; horizontalPoints/verticalPoints take two points; concentric takes two circular curves; tangent/smooth take two supported curves; equal takes two lines or two circular curves. The handler checks supported names and arity, leaving most API-type/solver compatibility to Fusion. Fixed state uses sketch.edit, not a fixed constraint mode.

sections.title: Return Contract
sections.text: result = {constraint:Ref}. Ref has token:string|null,kind:string,name:string|null, optional component/occurrence refs. Envelope {success,operation,document,result,created} includes this created constraint. No solved positions or DOF count is returned; run sketch.check/inspect. Solver failures propagate without rollback; no automatic removal of conflicting constraints.

examples.label: Horizontal discovered line
examples.requires: Create a nonfixed line in Section with sketch.geometry, then entity.alias its returned ref as SeedLine (or substitute that ref directly). Avoid an already-horizontal constrained line.
examples.output: result.constraint is the new native constraint ref.

verified: All fourteen dispatch names and arities
Endpoint selectors and solver delegation

sections.title: GM06 Ellipse Radius Dimensions
sections.text: majorRadius/minorRadius each take one SketchEllipse and use separate native SketchEllipseMajorRadiusDimension/SketchEllipseMinorRadiusDimension classes. Use the returned ellipse.majorAxis line from sketch.build for an angle dimension against an explicit reference line; angular text selects the quadrant. Linear distance values must be positive: signed center coordinates through zero use sketch.build positions and native datum bindings, not unsigned distance. Existing same-selection dimensions are rejected as duplicates; edit their expressions with sketch.edit dimensions. GM06 result adds schemaVersion/status/documentIdentity/units/frame/associativity and provenance. Native radius/loft acceptance remains open; see docs/GM06.md.

sections.title: Dimension Inputs
sections.text: Use the target sketch name/Ref and refs from sketch.inspect or sketch.geometry. Ref accepts {token,kind?,component?,occurrence?} or a real alias. distance requires two SketchPoints (endpoints can be {entity:curveRef,point:start|end|center}); angle requires two lines; radius/diameter one arc/circle. All entities must belong to the sketch. text is exactly three length-expression strings in sketch coordinates; it positions the annotation and selects the angular quadrant, not a driving coordinate. driving defaults true and requires expression:string (length except angle); driving:false forbids expression entirely. Only distance permits orientation:aligned(default)|horizontal|vertical. Expressions retain parameter equations on the created dimension; text coordinates are evaluated snapshots.

sections.title: Return Contract
sections.text: result = {dimension:Ref,parameter:string,expression:string}. expression is the actual parameter expression read back, including Fusion's measured expression for driven dimensions. Ref has token:string|null,kind:string,name:string|null and optional component/occurrence refs. Envelope {success,operation,document,result,created} appends the dimension ref. Feed result.parameter to param.inspect names with includeModel:true. Expression assignment happens after creation and may fail leaving a dimension; inspect before retry. No extra parameter-edit operation is implied.

examples.label: Driving diameter
examples.requires: SeedCircle is an entity.alias for a free circle in Section discovered from sketch.geometry result.refs.rim; omit an existing conflicting radial dimension.
examples.output: result.expression is the read-back driving expression and result.parameter is its model parameter name.

examples.label: Measured radius
examples.requires: Alias SeedCircle to an existing Section circle; expression must be omitted.
examples.output: result.expression reports the measured radius; geometry is not driven by this dimension.

verified: Legacy types, orientation and driving exclusivity
Separate ellipse major/minor dimensions and duplicate guards in fakes

sections.title: References And Linkage
sections.text: Target sketch is a unique name or Ref; obtain source refs through entity.list/entity.find or selection.inspect selections[i].entity. entities must be a nonempty array of supported source curves, points, BRep edges/vertices/faces/bodies or construction entities. Each ref is a unique alias or {token,kind?,component?,occurrence?}; preserve occurrence for intentional projection from an assembly instance. Unlike ordinary sketch constraints, source entities need not belong to the target sketch. linked is a JSON boolean, default true; false requests independent projection. Fusion project2 determines compatible inputs and projected multiplicity. No intersection/project-to-surface mode.

sections.title: Return Contract
sections.text: result = {entities:Ref[],refs:{}}. Ref has token:string|null,kind:string,name:string|null and optional component/occurrence refs. No source-to-output grouping or labels are returned; inspect returned entities to identify projected points/curves. Envelope {success,operation,document,result,created} appends projected entities. Batch p.result.entities.0 may feed a later sketch command. API project2 must exist; failures may leave partial geometry, with no rollback or save.

examples.label: Independent edge projection
examples.requires: Alias a real BRep edge from entity.list {kind:edge} as SelectedEdge, or replace it with the returned ref. Section exists and projection is geometrically suitable.
examples.output: result.entities lists projected geometry; refs is empty even if the source has an alias.

verified: Source scope differs from same-sketch constraints

sections.title: Connected Curves
sections.text: entities is a nonempty ordered array of curves belonging to sketch. Obtain actual refs from sketch.inspect curves or sketch.geometry refs; Ref is {token,kind?,component?,occurrence?} or a real unique alias. Supply the whole end-connected chain, not an automatic-discovery flag. distance is a signed length-expression string retained in the offset input; positive is right of curve flow (outward for a counterclockwise circle). Uses createOffsetInput/addOffset2 and childCurves, not retired Sketch.offset. No symmetric mode, end caps or topology repair; Fusion validates curve compatibility.

sections.title: Return Contract
sections.text: result = {constraint:Ref,entities:Ref[],refs:{},offsetParameter:string|null}. offsetParameter names the native offset dimension parameter (edit it with curve.offset-edit); null when the dimension is unavailable. entities are offset child curves, not input curves; refs has no labels. Ref has token:string|null,kind:string,name:string|null with optional component/occurrence refs. Envelope {success,operation,document,result,created} includes constraint and children. Batch o.result.entities.0 is usable in subsequent sketch commands. Creation/serialization failures may leave constraint/curves; inspect before retry, no rollback.

examples.label: Outward circular offset
examples.requires: SeedCircle must be an actual alias created with entity.alias for a Section circle returned by sketch.geometry; API must expose offset constraints.
examples.output: result.constraint is the native offset constraint; result.entities contains the child circle.

verified: Offset API argument list
Constraint and child return refs

sections.title: Geometry And Scope
sections.text: Resolve sketch and nonempty entities from sketch.inspect or sketch.geometry; refs are {token,kind?,component?,occurrence?} or existing unique aliases. line must resolve to a nonzero SketchLine in the same sketch. Only points, lines, circles and arcs are supported. Axis endpoints and source defining points must be in sketch XY (absolute z <=1e-7 cm). Geometry is reflected numerically, then native symmetry constraints are added. Arc endpoints reverse to preserve reflected traversal. Construction state is copied for curves; fixed state, dimensions and other constraints are not copied. No spline, ellipse, 3D or native mirror-pattern object.

sections.title: Return Contract
sections.text: result = {entities:Ref[],refs:{},constraints:Ref[]}; one new primitive and symmetry constraint per input in input order. Ref has token:string|null,kind:string,name:string|null and optional component/occurrence refs. Envelope {success,operation,document,result,created} records constraints and new geometry, not necessarily interleaved in geometric order. Use result.entities for next geometry selections. Planarity is prepared before mutation but kernel/constraint failures inside the loop can leave partial primitives; inspect before retry.

examples.label: Mirror circle about sketch axis
examples.requires: Use entity.alias on refs returned by sketch.geometry to create SeedCircle and MirrorAxis; both belong to Section, axis is a nonzero planar line, circle should not coincide with its mirror.
examples.output: result.entities[0] is the reflected circle and result.constraints[0] its symmetry constraint.

verified: All four reconstruction branches

sections.title: Conditional Inputs
sections.text: Select sketch and nonempty point/curve refs from sketch.inspect or sketch.geometry (returned refs or persistent aliases, not response labels). All subjects and direction/center entities belong to that sketch. circular requires center:SketchPoint ref and allows only angle beyond common fields, default 360 deg. rectangular requires distance:length-expression, permits distanceType:spacing(default)|extent and optional direction:SketchLine (omitted sketch X). quantityTwo and distanceTwo must appear together; directionTwo additionally requires that pair and otherwise defaults perpendicular to direction one. quantity is an integer >=1 or existing unitless parameter expression; booleans/floats reject. String quantities use generic expression validation, so integer/positivity compatibility is ultimately a Fusion check. Numeric literal strings such as "4" lack the required units/parameter reference; use integer 4. Extent/angle/distance expressions are retained, not coordinate copies.

sections.title: Return Contract
sections.text: result = {constraint:Ref}; no generated-entity array. Ref has token:string|null,kind:string,name:string|null and optional component/occurrence refs. Envelope {success,operation,document,result,created} appends the native pattern constraint. Run sketch.inspect again for generated curves. Native pattern-constraint API is required; no suppression/symmetry/compute options. Failures propagate with no rollback.

examples.label: Two-direction rectangular pattern
examples.requires: Alias a Section circle from sketch.geometry as SeedCircle. Ensure space for generated geometry and avoid conflicting constraints.
examples.output: result.constraint is the pattern; sketch.inspect returns the resulting geometry.

examples.label: Circular sketch pattern
examples.requires: SeedCircle and PatternCenter are actual aliases for a circle and SketchPoint in Section. Use sketch.geometry point output for center; do not use a coordinate array.
examples.output: result.constraint only; count includes the seed.

sections.title: Prerequisites And Meaning
sections.text: sketch is a unique existing name/alias or Ref from sketch.create or entity.list {kind:sketch}. Reads current state without activation/recompute and preserves explicit occurrence context. Underconstrained contains curves; underconstrainedPoints separately contains points. No degree-of-freedom count is claimed. Neither profile count nor full constraint proves gap-free/manufacturable geometry.

sections.title: Return Contract
sections.text: result includes sketch:Ref,isFullyConstrained:boolean,profileCount:integer,healthState:integer,message:string,underconstrained:Ref[],underconstrainedPoints:Ref[], plus GM06 schemaVersion/status/documentIdentity/units/frame/associativity and provenance. healthState is the native enum integer. Nonhealthy sketch state produces fail; underconstraint alone does not fail. created is empty. This is a health check, not design approval; inspect underconstrained refs rather than automatically fixing them.

examples.label: Read solver state
examples.requires: Existing Section sketch after the intended dimensions and constraints were applied.
examples.output: result.profileCount and result.isFullyConstrained report current state without recompute.

verified: Legacy status fields

sections.title: Path Descriptor
sections.text: Input is {curves:[Ref,...],chain?:none|connected|tangent,kind?:path,name?:nonblank string}. References are actual returned objects {token,kind?,component?,occurrence?} or existing aliases, obtained from sketch.geometry, sketch.inspect curves, entity.list {kind:edge}, or selection.inspect selections[i].entity. curves must be nonempty sketch curves/BRep edges with the same owner and occurrence. Automatic chaining needs exactly one seed; connected does not accept BRep edges. Native curves use owning component Features.createPath even if another component is selected; exact proxy context uses Path.create. No occurrence is inferred for native inputs. Connectivity, closure and branch feasibility remain Fusion checks.

sections.title: Return Contract
sections.text: result = {path:{kind:path,curves:Ref[],chain:none,name?:string},count:integer,isClosed:boolean}. Returned curves are ordered expanded path members, native for native requests and contextualized for explicit proxies. Ref has token:string|null,kind:string,name:string|null and optional component/occurrence refs. Envelope {success,operation,document,result,created} has created:[]; there is no timeline entity or persistent path alias. Batch p.result.path feeds model.sweep.path or pattern.path.path; path.inspect takes that descriptor itself as data, not {path:descriptor}. Model consumers require native selected-component paths, even though this read-only command can describe proxy paths.

examples.label: Discover connected sketch path
examples.requires: SeedLine is an actual entity.alias for a sketch curve from sketch.inspect; connected neighboring curves must form a valid path.
examples.output: result.path contains expanded refs and chain:none, reusable without relying on the label SweepPath.

verified: Native/proxy/owner scope and chaining branches
Descriptor normalization and downstream wiring

sections.title: Descriptor Input
sections.text: Accepts the fields of path.create result.path directly: {curves:[Ref,...],chain?:none|connected|tangent,kind?:path,name?:nonblank string}. Not {path:...} and not a path name. curves is nonempty; automatic chaining takes one seed, connected only sketch curves. Discover refs using sketch.inspect curves or entity.list {kind:edge}; refs are unique aliases or {token,kind?,component?,occurrence?}. Members must have one owner and one occurrence context; mixed native/proxy and cross-occurrence paths reject. Native owner-scoped reconstruction does not activate a component or invent an occurrence. Proxy paths retain the exact instance. This does not introspect partial ranges stored inside a sweep feature.

sections.title: Return Contract
sections.text: result = {path:{kind:path,curves:Ref[],chain:none,name?:string},count:integer,isClosed:boolean}. Ref has token:string|null,kind:string,name:string|null and optional component/occurrence refs (occurrence includes path:string). Envelope {success,operation,document,result,created} has created:[]; the Path is transient. Reuse result.path in native selected-component sweep/path-pattern inputs only if its curves are native in that component. Batch reference is p.result.path, not p.path. Kernel reconstruction can fail without model creation; closure is measured, not an input flag.

examples.label: Inspect explicit seed
examples.requires: SeedLine is a previously created alias for a real sketch curve. Alternatively substitute the entire path.create result.path object as this operation's data.
examples.output: result.count is the resolved member count; result.isClosed reports closure.

verified: Shared create/inspect implementation
No mutation and exact path output

sections.title: Profiles And Extents
sections.text: Exactly one of profile or profiles is required. profile accepts one Profile, planar BRepFace, or current-SDK SketchText ref; its selector may be {kind:profile,sketch:SketchRef,index:nonnegative integer}, or the exclusive loopCount:positive integer form. Omitting both requires exactly one sketch profile. profiles is the alternative nonempty ordered reference array; its members have the same selector forms. Resolve every ref before SDK input creation; reject duplicates, invalid refs, unsupported types, proxies, mixed owners/contexts, or any collection whose plane definitions are not co-planar. Profile plane, planar face geometry, or SketchText support plane is checked with the installed Fusion Plane API, not a guessed tolerance. Discover fresh profiles with sketch.inspect result.profiles[i].ref; indices can change after topology edits. Ref is a unique name/alias or {token,kind?,component?,occurrence?}. distance extent (default) requires distance and prohibits target/offset. throughAll prohibits distance/target/offset. toEntity requires target:construction-plane or face Ref, prohibits distance, allows offset default 0 mm. startOffset is a signed length expression in the profile plane, one-sided only; positive follows profile-plane Z independent of direction. direction is positive(default)|negative. symmetric:true uses full distance and prohibits direction/startOffset even if zero/default. taper defaults 0 deg; solid defaults true; operation newBody(default)|join|cut|intersect. participants are optional explicit owned native body refs for cut/intersect; omitted retains Fusion inference. Length/angle inputs use unit-bearing expressions or parameter expressions. No thin or independent two-sided mode.

sections.title: Multiple Profile Inputs
sections.text: Fusion ExtrudeFeatures.createInput accepts an ObjectCollection of co-planar Profiles, planar BRepFaces, or SketchText objects. The handler resolves all profile and participant refs, checks native selected-component ownership/context and coplanarity before creating that ObjectCollection or ExtrudeFeatureInput. profile and profiles are mutually exclusive; profiles:[] and duplicate refs reject. No cross-occurrence/proxy input, no open-profile helpers in the collection, and no mixed-plane collection. Coplanarity is compared in model coordinates: sketch-based profile planes are transformed into model space through the sketch transform before comparison, and planar-face or reference-plane geometry is already model space. A single profile keeps the legacy createInput(singleProfile,operation) path and existing result shape.

sections.title: Return Contract
sections.text: Single-profile result remains {feature:Ref,bodies:Ref[],healthState:integer,message:string}. Multi-profile results add profileRefs:Ref[] in caller input order, profileCount, bodyCount and profileBodyMapping:{status:unavailable,reason}. Every entry in bodies is an actual body Ref with its own token; bodyCount equals the returned bodies array length. Fusion exposes no stable body-to-input-profile mapping, so bodies array indices do not identify source profiles. The envelope {success,operation,document,result,created} records the feature in created, not each body. Bodies may be empty or differ in count from profiles for cut/join/intersect. Native ErrorFeatureHealthState raises after add instead of returning the success result. A warning health state is not accepted as success: a single-profile extrude returns it (healthState warning plus message) for the caller to check, while a multi-profile extrude raises on any non-healthy state including warning. Other SDK errors may leave partial changes; there is no automatic rollback.

sections.title: Scope And Failure
sections.text: Use native selected-component geometry and existing material for cut/join/intersect. Supplied participants must be explicit native bodies owned by the selected component; omitted cut/intersect participants preserve Fusion inference. Mutating execution activates the document, not the component, and never saves. No cross-occurrence creation. Conflicting input selectors, invalid refs, incompatible planes/contexts and unsupported geometry reject before feature input creation where preflight permits; kernel/name/health failures can still leave a feature or partial result, so inspect before retry. No auto-undo or source-input deletion.

examples.label: Distance solid
examples.requires: Section contains a closed profile selected from sketch.inspect in the native component. Base names the feature, not necessarily the body.
examples.output: result.feature is Base's feature ref; use its body token, not an assumed output index, when topology may change.

examples.label: Multi-profile cut with explicit target
examples.requires: CutSection has two disjoint, fresh, co-planar closed profiles in the same native component; Base is an actual body ref/alias from a preceding feature and intersects both profiles. N20_Depth is a length parameter. Multi-profile inputs are one native ObjectCollection; they are not individual sequential extrusions.
examples.output: result.profileCount is 2; profileRefs preserves the input selectors; bodies contains actual result refs and bodyCount. profileBodyMapping.status is unavailable, so no body-array position is assigned to a profile.

examples.label: Through-all cut
examples.requires: Base is a unique native body alias. Section intersects it in the negative profile-normal direction.
examples.output: result contains cut feature and affected body refs.

examples.label: Target extent
examples.requires: Create TargetPlane using datum.plane at a finite offset beyond Section in the same component; inspect both supports.
examples.output: result.feature retains start and target-offset expressions.

sections.title: Inputs And Scope
sections.text: Discover section selectors with sketch.inspect result.profiles[i].ref: {kind:profile,sketch:Ref,index:integer}; no index requires one profile, loopCount optionally selects one matching loop count instead of index. All geometry must be native in selected component; the shared owner guard checks construction datums through .component and rejects foreign native datums and explicit geometry proxies before SDK feature input creation or add.

Ref = unique existing alias or {token,kind?,component?,occurrence?}; native selected-component inputs only. orientation:perpendicular(default)|parallel, twist and taper angle-expression strings are all forbidden when guideRail is present, even at defaults. Rail uses native default scaling. operation:newBody(default)|join|cut|intersect; solid:boolean default true; participants:nonempty body refs only cut/intersect. Expressions retain feature equations, not route coordinate generation. No solid-body sweep, guide surface or rail flip controls.

sections.text: Supply exactly one of edges or query. query is the entity.find version-1 grammar, default kind edge; expect or unique:true is mandatory. All matches are resolved and count/owner/nonempty guards checked before SDK feature input creation. radius must evaluate to a positive length. Successful result adds resolvedQuery (the full pre-mutation query snapshot) and selectionAssociativity:snapshot. TangentChain may expand these seeds inside Fusion; returned refs are not a promise of topology stability or an associative future query. See docs/ENTITY_QUERIES.md for native fixture and pending acceptance.

sections.text: edges is a nonempty native reference array, usually BRep edges from entity.list {kind:edge}, entity.find or selection.inspect selections[i].entity. Face/feature subjects select associated edges only as Fusion's edge-set API supports; this wrapper does not expand them itself. Ref = unique actual alias or {token,kind?,component?,occurrence?}. radius is a length-expression string retained in one constant-radius edge set; tangentChain:boolean defaults true. Native selected-component geometry only. No variable/full-round/face-fillet mode, multiple radius sets or operation field. Edge topology may change after prior operations; rediscover rather than guessing indices/tokens.

sections.title: Return Contract
